data.title: Senator Lummis: CLARITY Act could aid crypto firms in hacks like $6B Binance incident
data.description:
Senator Cynthia Lummis highlighted the potential impact of the stalled CLARITY Act on cryptocurrency regulation, specifically in the context of the recent $6.3 billion hack targeting Binance. She noted that the act would have provided legal backing for crypto firms to freeze assets immediately upon request from law enforcement. This statement follows an incident where Binance coordinated with authorities, managing to freeze approximately $3 billion of the affected assets. The CLARITY Act, which seeks to formalize such collaborations, remains under consideration by lawmakers, with its future still uncertain.

  • Senator Lummis's comments suggest the CLARITY Act could enhance cooperation between crypto firms and law enforcement.
  • Market pricing indicates the act's passage could influence key votes, potentially increasing support from undecided senators.
  • Current odds reflect a slight increase in the likelihood of Senator Mike Lee voting in favor of the CLARITY Act.

Observers should monitor any further statements from key senators, such as Mike Lee, who could be swayed by the implications of Lummis's remarks. Any developments regarding the scheduling of a vote on the CLARITY Act in the Senate will be crucial. Additionally, watch for any public endorsements or criticisms from influential political figures that could shift market perceptions of the act's viability.

data.title: Fitch Affirms Slovakia at ’A-’ with Stable Outlook
data.description:
Fitch Ratings affirmed Slovakia’s long-term foreign-currency Issuer Default Rating at A- with a Stable Outlook on October 30, 2026, citing the country’s deep integration with the euro area and continued EU fund inflows despite mounting budget pressures.

However, fiscal consolidation is expected to lose momentum ahead of the 2027 parliamentary election, with the deficit projected to widen to 5.0% of GDP in 2027 before improving from 2028.

The deterioration reflects higher public-sector wages, social spending, defense expenditure, and debt-servicing costs.

Still, an average debt maturity of over eight years helps contain near-term refinancing risks.

GDP growth is projected to grow by 0.8% in 2026 amid higher energy prices and financing costs linked to Middle East tensions.

Growth is forecast to strengthen gradually to 1.8% by 2028, on rising automotive production and stronger investment.

Other major agencies keep stable outlooks, with S&P rating Slovakia A, Moody’s A3, and DBRS A (low).

data.title: Bank holiday today 31 Oct 2026: Are banks open today? Check if SBI, HDFC, ICICI Bank and others are open in your city
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- Bank branches across most parts of India will remain open today, Saturday, 31 October 2026. However, customers in Gujarat will have to account for a regional bank holiday marking the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

Although 31 October falls on a Saturday, it is the fifth Saturday of the month. Under the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) banking holiday rules, all scheduled and non-scheduled banks remain closed on the second and fourth Saturdays, while other Saturdays are regular working days unless a separate state-specific holiday has been declared.

Here's what you need to know about bank closures in your city today, 31 October 2026.

Banks in Gujarat will remain closed on 31 October on account of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birthday. The holiday is included in the Gujarat government's official bank holiday calendar for 2026.

The Government of Gujarat notified the list of public holidays for banks in the state for 2026 under Notification No. GS/22/2025/JSR/2025/509/GH, dated 27 November 2025.

The notification states: "The Government of Gujarat, in consultation with Reserve Bank of India, Ahmedabad, is pleased to declare the following days to be public holidays for banks in Gujarat during the year 2026."

It specifically lists Saturday, 31 October 2026, as a public holiday for banks on account of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birthday.

This means bank branches in Ahmedabad and all parts of Gujarat will remain closed today. The holiday applies to both public-sector and private-sector bank branches in the state, including SBI, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank.

According to the RBI holiday calendar, banks will operate normally in Bengaluru, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Chennai, Jaipur, Jammu, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, New Delhi, Patna, Thiruvananthapuram, etc.

These cities or states do not have a separate bank holiday notified for 31 October 2026. Since the date is the fifth Saturday, the regular second- and fourth-Saturday closure rule does not apply.

Yes. State-specific bank holidays apply only to banks operating in the notified region.

Therefore, SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Bank of Baroda, Punjab National Bank, Axis Bank, and other lenders will keep their branches open today, except in Gujarat.

data.title: Ramalinga Raju who went for a ride on a tiger and stopped smiling thereafter
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- In 2008, Ramalinga Raju had the world at his feet. India's IT industry was poised for take-off, following the boost from the turn-of-the-century Y2K scare, which sent global corporations scrambling to Indian vendors for fixes to their software programmes. The threat proved largely a red herring, but the discovery of Indian IT talent was real. India's software exports had soared from $6.3 billion in 2000-01 to $47 billion in 2008-09, and despite the financial crisis, the long-term outlook was bright.

Satyam Computer Services, the company Raju had founded in 1987, was among the front-runners of this boom. It had closed the previous year with reported revenues of Rs.8,473 crore and profits of Rs.1,688 crore, ranking fourth among India's IT services companies. Its 1992 IPO had rewarded shareholders handsomely, with the stock touching a peak of Rs.544 in May 2008.

Then January 2009 dawned, and another familiar story of entrepreneurial ambition collapsing under the weight of corporate deception burst into the open.

Byrraju Ramalinga Raju, from Bhimavaram in coastal Andhra Pradesh, was an unlikely IT czar. Born into an agricultural family, he graduated in commerce before earning an MBA from Ohio University. On returning to India in 1977, he tried his hand at textiles and construction before starting Satyam with his brother-in-law DVS Raju and just 20 employees. The company surged, eventually employing more than 50,000 people and serving blue-chip clients including General Electric, Nestle and Cisco.

Raju was soon the toast of the industry, serving on prominent industry bodies and chairing Nasscom in 2006-07. Meanwhile, his family ventured into real estate and infrastructure, businesses that would become crucial to his downfall.

On 7 January 2009, Raju stunned investors with a confessional letter admitting that Satyam's books had been systematically cooked. They contained thousands of crores in fictitious cash and bank balances, accrued interest and inflated debtors, alongside large hidden liabilities. The reported operating profit for the September 2008 quarter was Rs.649 crore, while the actual figure was just Rs.61 crore. The gap, he admitted, had grown beyond his ability to manage.

In his letter, he captured the trap he had created for himself: "It was like riding a tiger, not knowing how to get off without being eaten."

The immediate trigger was a proposal for Satyam to buy 100% of the family firm Maytas Properties for $1.3 billion and take a 51% stake in Maytas Infrastructure for $300 million. The deal made little strategic sense for Satyam and appeared to offer a way of converting the company's purported cash reserves into tangible assets owned by the promoter family. Raju later acknowledged that the acquisition was a last-ditch attempt to cover fictitious assets with real ones.

The board approved the proposal, but investors reacted furiously to what they saw as a blatant conflict of interest. The deal was withdrawn the next day. Satyam's American depositary receipts plunged, while the backlash was compounded by the World Bank's decision to bar the company from certain business for improper benefits and the departure of independent directors.

The global financial crisis and a deteriorating outlook for IT spending added to the pressure. The final push came when investment bank DSP Merrill Lynch, engaged to explore ways of enhancing shareholder value, flagged financial discrepancies and alerted the market regulator.

The Maytas fiasco did not create the fraud; it exposed the desperation behind it. The Central Bureau of Investigation later uncovered thousands of fabricated invoices, while scrutiny revealed that even Satyam's reported headcount and operating performance had been exaggerated. The company's stock collapsed, wiping out Rs.13,655 crore of shareholder wealth.

Raju resigned on 7 January and was arrested two days later, along with his brother and Satyam managing director, B. Rama Raju. The government dissolved the board and appointed new directors to stabilise the company.

In April 2015, a special CBI court convicted Ramalinga Raju and nine others in the fraud case, sentencing them to seven years' imprisonment. Separately, Sebi imposed a 14-year market ban. The audit partners also faced disciplinary action, even as the independence and oversight of auditors came under scrutiny. Raju was granted bail after his conviction, with his sentence suspended pending appeal. He has since largely withdrawn from public life.

Satyam itself disappeared into the folds of Tech Mahindra, which bought the stricken company following a government-supervised bidding process in 2009. But the Satyam name has become synonymous with corporate fraud.

Had Ramalinga Raju stayed the course with India's IT story, he could have made billions. Instead, he chose to ride a tiger.

For more such stories, read The Enterprising Indian: Stories From India Inc.

data.title: Here's why Granules India shares could see a reaction on Monday
data.description:
Granules India shares will be in focus on Monday (November 2) after the company reported that the US FDA has issued Form 483 to the company's Hyderabad Unit with 11 observations after concluding a GMP inspection at a Hyderabad facility. This confirms the CNBC-TV18 newsbreak. Earlier on October 19, CNBC-TV18 had reported that the US FDA began an audit of Gagillapur. CNBC-TV18 had reached out to Granules for a comment.

CNBC-TV18 Newsbreak Confirmed

In an exchange filing issued on Saturday, October 31, the company said that the United States Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) concluded a current Good Manufacturing Practice inspection of its finished dosage facility at Gagillapur, Hyderabad. The inspection, as mentioned before, concluded with the issuance of Form 483 with a total of 11 observations.

The said inspection was conducted from October 19 to October 30, 2026.

As per the US drug regulator, an FDA Form 483 is issued to a company when an FDA investigator has observed any violations of the Food, Drug and Cosmetic (FD&C) Act and related Acts.

Observations are conducted when, in the investigator's assessment, the conditions or practices noted suggest that any food, drug, device, or cosmetic has been adulterated or is being prepared, packaged, or stored in a manner that could lead to adulteration or pose a health risk.

Company's Reaction

The Telangana-based company said that this was the first USFDA inspection of the facility since the Warning Letter of February 26, 2025, which followed an inspection in August-September 2024.

For its part, the company has claimed that none of the observations was related to data integrity or cross-contamination.

Furthermore, according to Granules, the observations concern the enhancements in investigations, change control, process and equipment qualification, visual-inspection controls and documentation practices.

The company further added that there is no impact on manufacturing or distribution of products from the site. In addition, Granules also added that the company will submit a 'comprehensive' response to the US drug agency within 15 days.

Commenting on the inspection, Dr. Krishna Prasad Chigurupati, Chairman and Managing Director, said: “The inspection progressed constructively, and the observations are of a nature that we believe can be fully addressed through our responses and corrective and preventive actions. Quality is the foundation of everything we do at Granules, and we will continue to engage transparently with the agency.”

Ahead Of Q2 Results

The company will be reporting its results for the second quarter or Q2FY27 on November 2. Ahead of that, when we look at its performance in Q1, the pharma company's Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) for the June quarter rose by 37.4% YoY to ₹339 crore from ₹246.5 crore.

The EBITDA margin expanded by over 300 basis points to 23% from 20.3% YoY. Granules India's net profit for the period increased by 60% year-on-year to ₹180 crore from ₹112.60 crore. Revenue grew 22% to ₹1,476 crore from ₹1,210 crore during Q1 of FY26.

Stock Performance

When we look at the performance of the pharma company's stock, the shares of the company closed in the green on Friday, with minimal gains of 0.29%. In this year's trade so far, the stock price has expanded its value by over 35%.

Furthermore, the stock is at over 9% below its 52-week high of ₹923.65 and sitting with a cushion of 58.49% above its 52-week low of ₹529.85. The stock has made major gains over the past week and has closed in the green in 7 out of the last 10 trading sessions.

data.title: Can India afford tax cuts right now?
data.description:
With just about three months to the budget, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman is likely to be swamped with demands for more funds or tax relief. One of the loudest is the clamour for a cut in long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) and securities transaction tax (STT). Stock investors argue that a tax cut will bring back foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) who have yanked out a staggering $32.5 billion from Indian equities this year.

The big question for Sitharaman is whether the exchequer can afford tax cuts amidst rising expenses and ballooning debt.

There's an estimated ₹2.85 lakh crore fiscal hole as subsidy bills surge and tax collections slide, according to ICRA, a Mumbai-based ratings agency. That's more than double the revenue from LTCG in the financial year ended March 2025.

How bad could India's balance of payments get? 

Meanwhile, the dollar exodus from the share market has worsened the country's balance of payments (BoP), the difference between money coming into the country and the sum that leaves. A net outflow of money of $50 billion to $55 billion in the second half of the year could keep the rupee under pressure, says Madhavi Arora, chief economist at Emkay Global, a Mumbai broking firm.

The Reserve Bank of India has already spent $67 billion over the last 8 weeks to keep the rupee afloat. That's nearly half of the $144 billion ammunition parked with Indian banks, and subsidised by the regulator, which would be due for repayment in less than three years.

"Excluding FCNR(B), you would be looking at, you know, multiple years of a BOP deficit, which becomes a source of, let's say, financial stability risks and all of that," Dhiraj Nim said.

"Unlike the last time this happened around 2013, this is not so much a homegrown problem. This is happening because of certain global factors which have weighed on flows into India."DHIRAJ NIM, ECONOMIST, ANZ

If the FPI selling continues, and the government remains intent on not letting the currency slide to ₹100/dollar, the RBI will have to spend even more of its forex reserves.

LTCG hike didn't start the FPI sell-off, a cut may not stop it

Indeed, the sell-off in Indian stocks started in the fall of 2024 because Indian stocks had run up too much, too fast, and global investors found them expensive. There were juicy profits to be taken out of India, and the AI trade in other countries offered the investors a relatively lucrative opportunity to put their capital to work. Then came the US-Iran war, which drove up oil prices past the $100 mark, squeezing vulnerable economies like India.

Stock valuations have corrected enough already, and an LTCG cut in India will not stop the US-Iran war, nor will it birth large language models or memory chip makers overnight.

Pain relief for a few, austerity for many 

It may offer some pain relief to bleeding portfolios, but the government has other responsibilities too. "The government is cutting expenses elsewhere. For example, some of the water scheme, some of the housing scheme, and so on and so forth," HSBC's Pranjul Bhandari said. These cuts affect the poorer sections of society, most of whom may not have a stake in the stock market.

Cutting spending on essentials when inflation is rising may be politically costly. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's rivals would have more material to escalate their attacks on the administration.

The country has less than 63 million unique people with investments in mutual funds, according to the August data released by the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI). A much larger base of voters with no investable surplus is reeling from the high cost of food, fuel, and fertilisers.

The government has already seen its tax revenue dip 23% in the first five months of this fiscal year due to duty cuts in petrol and diesel. ICRA expects the fiscal deficit (the difference between the government's expenses and revenue) to be at least ₹1.3 lakh more than what it had budgeted for in February this year. That's as much as the LTCG collected in FY25.

A tax cut may bring some dollars back, for a while. It may help some portfolios, but as a result, the fiscal deficit would look bad, which is, again, not something FPIs like.

The end of the war in West Asia would be enough to spur a sharp correction in oil prices, which would in turn reduce inflation, cap the cost of capital, and improve earnings growth for Indian companies, making them attractive again for FPIs. That's a tide the Indian government can't turn.

data.title: Ex-SC Judge to Mediate Dispute Between Govt & RIL Consortium Over K-G Gas
data.description:
Indu Bhan New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday appointed former judge Ranjana Prakash Desai as the sole mediator to resolve the long-running $1.73 billion Krishna-Godavari basin gas migration dispute between a Reliance Industries-led consortium and the government, after the two sides failed to reach an amicable settlement in the case.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M Pancholi referred the matter for mediation after attorney general R Venkataramani informed that the parties were unable to arrive at a "viable solution". The bench said Justice Desai, a former judge of the top court, could take assistance from two domain experts as may be suggested by the parties to facilitate the mediation process.

The two sides assured the court that they would extend full cooperation to the mediator. The court will take up the case again after four weeks and check the progress of the mediation. The SC was hearing three appeals filed by Reliance Industries and its partners- BP Exploration (Alpha) of the UK and Canada-based Niko (NECO) - against a February 2025 decision of the Delhi High Court, which set aside a 2018 international arbitration ruling favouring the consortium in the dispute. The high court held that the arbitration award was contrary to the settled position of law.

data.title: Inflation, Poor Monsoon Hurt Liquor Spends: USL
data.description:
Aanya Thakur Mumbai: Inflation and a weaker monsoon are weighing on lower-income urban consumers, posing a challenge for United Spirits as the Diageo-controlled liquor maker seeks to revive growth in its mass-market portfolio while banking on premiumisation to drive sales. "India 1, the bottom end, the India 1 consumer, which is a target audience for the lower half of the IMFL portfolio, is showing signs of fatigue due to the impact of inflation on their wallets," chief executive Praveen Someshwar said during the company's September-quarter earnings call. "India 2 and India 3 are robust and holding up." The strain is also visible in the company's lower-priced portfolio, where regulatory changes are adding additional pressures.

United Spirits' popular segment reported a 22.7% decline in net sales value to 181 crore in the quarter, accounting for about 6% of revenue. The business was hit by adverse policy changes in Maharashtra and Karnataka.

The company's prestige and above portfolio grew 6%, making up 94% of revenue. The Smirnoff maker said it has no immediate plans to intervene in its popular portfolio, largely comprising McDowell's rum, even as CFO Pradeep Jain acknowledged that future profit and growth pools lay in higher-priced brands. "The category will probably die a natural death, so as of now we don't want to make any interventions," he added.

Cost inflation is another pressure point. The West Asia conflict has added about 50 crore to costs in the quarter, affecting glass, energy, packaging and logistics. Extra neutral alcohol prices have also started rising on account of El NiÃ±o's impact on monsoons and crop inflation, the company said.

It expects lower Scotch import duties under the India-UK free trade agreement to offset the ENA cost in the coming quarter. "Hopefully, this will be neutralised by the full effect of the FTA benefit," said Jain, adding that impact beyond the next quarter was "very difficult to call out." The FTA benefit comes amid a directorate of revenue intelligence investigation into the classification of Scotch imports.

data.title: JioStar Net Declines 13% to 1,147 crore in Sept Quarter
data.description:
Mumbai: JioStar, the media and entertainment arm of Reliance Industries (RIL), reported a 13.2% year-on-year fall in net profit to 1,147 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, against 1,322 crore a year earlier.

Gross revenue rose 9.8% to 7,944 crore, while revenue from operations increased 10.1% to 6,806 crore, according to RIL's investor presentation. However, Ebitda from operations fell 10.5% to 1,372 crore. Operating Ebitda margin contracted 600 basis points to 22.1%. Total Ebitda, including investment income, declined 13.6% to 1,502 crore.

JioHotstar averaged around 440 million monthly active users during the quarter, up 10% year-on-year, while entertainment watch-time grew more than 15%. Active subscribers in Singapore, the UK and Canada rose around 30% following the platform's September relaunch in these markets.

JioHotstar introduced "Pay Kisi Aur Se" or "Ask Others to Pay", allowing subscribers to ask friends or family to complete their payments. The company said the feature led to a 10% increase in incremental payment initiations. It also extended CTV access to mobile plan users, with viewing limited to two hours a month. The six editions of 'Bigg Boss' collectively reached more than 90 million viewers in their first three weeks.

data.title: FNCR Flows Mask Banks' Deposit Woes
data.description:
An analysis of 10 banks shows that deposit growth averaged 21.1% YoY during July-September. But it was estimated at 12.2% on excluding FCNR(B) inflows, reflecting weaker deposit mobilisation. Saloni Shukla reports. 8 growth weak at 12.2% after excluding foreign currency windfall Saloni Shukla Mumbai: The sharp rebound in bank deposit growth during the September quarter appears to mask continued difficulties in domestic deposit mobilisation, as the growth was temporarily inflated by the Reserve Bank of India's special Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) swap window.

An analysis of 10 banks shows that reported deposit growth averaged 21.1% year-on-year during July-September. However, excluding the special foreign currency inflows, domestic deposit growth was estimated at just 12.2%-a massive gap of nearly nine percentage points. A similar trend was seen in lending. Reported credit growth averaged 24.2%, but excluding loans linked to the central bank's special window, it was an estimated 18.9%, a difference of more than five percentage points.

The divergence suggests that underlying deposit mobilisation remains weaker than headline numbers indicate, particularly as growth in low-cost current and savings account deposits continues to lag overall deposit growth. At the banking-system level, RBI data showed that deposit growth of 17.8% at September-end continued to trail credit growth of 19.4%, despite extraordinary foreign-currency inflows. Deposit growth subsequently moderated to 16.7% by October 15, while credit growth remained higher at 18.2%. Credit-deposit ratio stood at 81.6%. Among individual lenders, RBL Bank reported deposit growth of 34% during the quarter, which moderated to just 6% when FCNR (B) deposits were excluded.

Kotak Mahindra Bank's deposit growth fell to 13% from 23.2%, while ICICI Bank's declined to 17% from 27.1%. HDFC Bank reported 18.8% deposit growth, including a four-percentage-point contribution from the special window.

The impact was also visible on the lending side. ICICI Bank's reported advances growth of 30% moderated to 24.1% after excluding FCNR(B)-backed lending, while Axis Bank's growth of about 23% fell to nearly 19% on its adjusted measure. The special window, which closed on August 31, helped banks collectively mobilise nearly $133 billion in FCNR (B) deposits.

Banks are now looking to deploy the surplus liquidity into fresh lending over the next two quarters while simultaneously reducing their reliance on expensive wholesale deposits and borrowings. "We are carrying some amount of excess liquidity currently, and I would expect that to be kind of deployed over the next two quarters," Anindya Banerjee, chief financial officer at ICICI Bank, said during the lender's September-quarter earnings call. Kotak Mahindra Bank similarly expects its FCNR (B)liquidity to support incremental lending over the coming quarters, in addition to growth funded by regular deposits. "The FCNR (B) deployment will be in addition to the core deployment from the core deposit," said Devang Gheewalla, group chief financial officer at Kotak Mahindra Bank. He indicated that the bank would deploy the remaining liquidity into customer assets over the next few quarters.

RBL Bank is also looking to expand its wholesale and secured retail businesses using the additional liquidity. The bank has already used part of the funds to retire expensive borrowings and bulk deposits, while temporarily deploying the balance into short-term investments and corporate loans.The inflows have temporarily eased competition for domestic deposits.

According to the RBI's October Bulletin, weighted average rates on fresh domestic term deposits moderated by 40 basis points during April-August, driven partly by foreign-currency inflows and surplus liquidity. A basis point is a hundredth of a percentage point. However, the underlying challenge of building granular deposit franchises remains. With the special FCNR (B) deposit window now closed, the challenge for lenders will be to sustain domestic deposit mobilisation while funding continued demand for corporate, working-capital and retail loans. RBI data showed that deposit growth of 17.8% at Sept-end continued to trail credit growth of 19.4%

data.title: JK Lakshmi Cement Launches Assam Project
data.description:
Bikash Singh Guwahati: JK Lakshmi Cement, held the groundbreaking of Project 'Kamakshi', its first footprint in Assam, at Umrangso village in Dima Hasao district on Friday. Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma attended the event.

Project Kamakshi will be an integrated cement plant with railway sidings. The plant will have a cement capacity of 2.5 million tonnes per annum, supported by a 1 million tonne clinkerisation unit, and is being developed with a total investment of 11,000 crore, including the mining lease. The project is targeted for completion by FY 2029. and will have a future workforce of over 2,000 people, catering primarily to the North East market.

Vinita Singhania, chairperson and managing director, JK Lakshmi Cement, said, "Project Kamakshi is the start of a long-term relationship with Assam and the wider Northeast. This is a region that is building fast, and it deserves quality cement made close to home. With this plant, we want to bring scale, jobs, and dependable supply to the region.

data.title: Delhivery Swings to Black as Revenue Rises 20% in 2nd Qtr
data.description:
Our Bureau New Delhi: New-age logistics company Delhivery reported a 20% year-on-year increase in its operating revenue at 3,066 crore for the September quarter, led by growth in its transport services business. This comprises its ecommerce shipment and part-truck load transportation verticals.

The Gurugram-based company posted a net profit of 41 crore during the three month period, compared to a 50 crore net loss in the same quarter last year. The turnaround in Delhivery's bottomline was consistent with its improving unit economics over the last few quarters.

In the April-June period, it reported 32 crore in net profit. Express parcel, or the ecommerce shipment business, reported a 32% year-on-year volume growth and a 22% revenue growth during the September quarter. This is Delhivery's biggest business vertical. "Express volumes grew 32% YoY in Q2FY27 and 43% YoY in H1FY27, reflecting continued market share gains and the strength of our value proposition across a broad and diversified customer base.

While it remains early to comment on the remainder of Q3FY27, October volumes have exceeded our initial expectations, providing an encouraging start to Q3," the company said in its letter to the shareholders. The October-December quarter of 2026 is expected to be a strong period for logistics and ecommerce companies given that most of the festive shopping period falls during these months.

Delhivery said it will focus on four key initiatives to sustain growth through the rest of FY27 and beyond. These include expanding the geographic reach of its same-day and next-day delivery network, deepening adoption of its integrated warehousing and transportation services among ecommerce clients, and broadening its aggregator and franchise partner programmes.

The company also plans to introduce new products and value-added services on its Delhivery One and Delhivery Direct platforms to onboard more small and medium enterprises (SMEs), micro-SMEs and individual consumers. Delhivery's listed rival Shadowfax on Thursday reported a 57% year-on-year (YoY) increase in operating revenue to 1,538 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with 982 crore in the year-ago period.

Its net profit rose fivefold to 68 crore in Q2 of the 2027 fiscal compared to 13 crore reported a year earlier. During the company's earnings call, Delhivery's CEO Sahil Barua said it will keep investing in growth while continuing to gain market share in the third-party logistics market.

data.title: PB Fintech Q2 Profit Rises 43% to 192cr
data.description:
Our Bureau Bengaluru: PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, reported a 43% year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit to 192.39 crore in the September quarter, driven by strong growth in its core insurance marketplace business and higher renewal income, even as the company continued investing in newer businesses.

Net profit stood at 134.89 crore a year earlier. Sequentially, profit increased 18% from 162.91 crore in the June quarter. Revenue from operations grew 35% to 2,177.71 crore from 1,613.55 crore a year prior. On a sequential basis, revenue increased 15% from 1,888.28 crore. The growth was led by Policybazaar's insurance distribution business, where demand for health and term insurance remained strong.

Total insurance premiums rose 38% to 9,385 crore, with new protection premiums increasing 42%. New health insurance premiums grew 46% YoY. Revenue from its core online businesses, comprising Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, increased 39% to 1,336 crore. Within this, insurance revenue rose 42% to 1,211 crore, while credit revenue grew 19% to 125 crore.

Renewal and trail revenue, which represents recurring income from existing insurance and credit customers, increased 42% to 1,097 crore on a trailing 12-month basis. This has become an important contributor to profitability as the company's customer base expands. Paisabazaar's core loan disbursements rose 22% to 2,791 crore, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of sequential growth.

Meanwhile, revenue from newer initiatives grew 28% to 842 crore, led by its offline insurance distribution platform PB Partners and international operations. PB Partners' revenue rose 39% to 698 crore, while its active advisor network expanded 55% to 131,000.

However, adjusted Ebitda (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation) losses in newer businesses widened to 42 crore from 27 crore, reflecting investments including in PB Pay and Pensionbazaar. At the consolidated level, adjusted Ebitda increased 39% to 216 crore. Total expenses rose 33% to 2,067.66 crore, with advertising and promotional expenditure climbing 59%. Revenue UP Revenue from operations grew 35% to 2,177.71 crore from 1,613.55 crore a yr prior

data.title: Omron Making in Chennai, Soon for the World
data.description:
Rica Bhattacharyya Mumbai: Omron Healthcare aims to establish Chennai as an international manufacturing hub, said its president and CEO Ayumu Okada, even though the Japanese maker of blood pressure monitors and nebulisers has earmarked the initial output from its newly established Indian facility near the Tamil Nadu capital for domestic sales.

The Kyoto-headquartered company, which has started full-scale production at its first manufacturing facility in India near Chennai, is aiming to reach an annual capacity of 3 million blood pressure monitors by 2028, as it looks to tap the country's largely underpenetrated home blood pressure monitoring market. "India remains an important growth market for us, with significant opportunities to expand home blood pressure monitoring," Okada said. "During the initial phase, 100% of the factory's production output will be allocated to the Indian domestic market." The immediate priority, she said, is to supply products tailored to the needs of Indian consumers in a timely manner, "helping promote wider adoption of home blood pressure monitoring and contributing to efforts to address the country's cardiovascular health challenges". "Over the medium to long term, Omron Healthcare aims to develop Chennai into a manufacturing base supplying healthcare devices to international markets, while strengthening the flexibility and resilience of its global manufacturing network," Okada said.

Despite India's substantial hypertension burden, fewer than 5% of Indian households regularly use a home blood pressure monitor, she said. According to the company's estimates, Omron Healthcare held about 40% of India's home blood pressure monitor market in 2025.

India accounted for around 3% of its global sales in the year ended March 2026. The company's Chennai facility, spanning nearly 24,000 square metres, started full-scale production this month. It has five production lines manufacturing five blood pressure monitor models for the Indian market.

The company has not disclosed the investment in the facility or its expected first-year production volumes. The company is also looking to increase domestic sourcing of components. The Chennai factory carries out assembly through to finished blood pressure monitors in India, drawing on production technologies and quality-control expertise developed at its facilities in Japan and Vietnam. "We are continuing to identify and develop relationships with local suppliers to increase the proportion of components sourced domestically, supporting the government's Make in India initiative," Okada said. Local manufacturing is expected to improve logistical efficiencies and strengthen domestic supply, although the company has not committed to specific retail price reductions.

data.title: Tata Motors Gets Control of Iveco With 89.4 % Stake
data.description:
Our Bureau New Delhi: Tata Motors, formerly TML Commercial Vehicle Business, Friday said it has completed the initial settlement of its tender offer for Iveco Group, acquiring a controlling 89.42% stake in the Italian commercial vehicle maker and making it an indirect subsidiary.

In a regulatory filing, Tata Motors said its wholly owned arm TML CV Holdings BV now holds 238,157,212 common shares of Iveco Group, net of treasury shares. The all-cash offer was priced at 14.4 per share. The deal marks a major global push for Tata Motors. Iveco, listed in Milan and headquartered in Amsterdam, employs 33,000 people across 16 industrial sites and 22 R&D centres.

Its brands include Iveco trucks, powertrain specialist FPT, bus makers Iveco Bus and Heuliez, and the financing arm Iveco Capital. Iveco reported revenue of 13.43 billion (about 1.42 lakh crore) in 2025, down from 14.42 billion in 2024 and 15.98 billion in 2023.

The 2023 figure includes defence business that is not part of the current transaction. Tata Motors said the offer brings together two businesses with highly complementary product portfolios and capabilities, with substantially no overlap in industrial and geographic footprints. The company said this would create a stronger, more diversified entity with a significant global presence.

It added that the acquisition is not a related party transaction. Following the acquisition, Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran has become chairperson of the Iveco board. Tata Motors executives P B Balaji and Girish Wagh have joined as non-independent directors, while Guenter Butschek and Charles Nichols will serve as independent directors.

Olof Persson will continue as chief executive. Charles Nichols will chair the audit committee, while Butschek will head the compensation committee and Wagh the ESG committee. Iveco has also adopted amended corporate governance documents. All outstanding special voting shares were repurchased for no consideration, following approval at an extraordinary general meeting on October 16, leaving none outstanding.

The acceptance period will reopen for five trading days from November 2 to 6, allowing remaining shareholders to tender at the same price. Shares tendered then will be settled on November 13. Tata Motors said it will announce post-offer steps in due course. Depending on the final stake, this could include a voluntary purchase procedure, a Dutch legal squeeze-out, or a post-offer demerger and liquidation, as set out in the offer document.

data.title: NDA Revived IDBI Bank After UPA-era Bad Loan Crisis: FM
data.description:
Our Bureau New Delhi: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman Friday countered Rahul Gandhi's opposition to the privatisation of IDBI Bank, saying the NDA government turned around a lender that had sunk into a bad-loan sinkhole due to questionable underwriting during the erstwhile UPA regime. "IDBI Bank was handed over to us in poor shape, as IDBI itself was forced to lend to large business groups with close connections to @INCIndia leaders such as Videocon, Winsome, ABG Shipyard, Kingfisher, etc.

These turned into bad loans, causing huge losses for IDBI Bank, which we recognised," the finance minister wrote on social media platform X (formerly, Twitter). Her response came after Gandhi, leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, said in a post on X that he stood with the employees of IDBI Bank against the stake sale and that during the strategic sale process, first the bids were seen and then the price was set.

Canadian investor Fairfax is set to take over IDBI Bank in the biggest cross-border M&A to date in Indian banking. In her response, Sitharaman noted that the NDA govt led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi revived the IDBI Bank through professionalism, prudence and recapitalisation of more than 25,000 crore. "The IDBI Bank is now poised for its next phase of growth," she said, noting that all due process has been followed in the IDBI Bank strategic restructuring.

The finance minister in her response stated that during Congress-era, banking had become a phonebook for the powerful and a rulebook for the common citizens. "The era of 'connection and setting banking' is over. Common people now have easy access to loans, and employees are not under pressure to extend loans over the phone calls," she said.

The finance minister in her response noted that, "@INCIndia has used banks and financial institutions as personal entities and pressured bank employees to extend loans at their whim, bypassing prudent lending norms." She also listed past instances, including that of Pawan Kumar Bansal, as a minister in the UPA, pressured Canara Bank to give loans to his family-linked businesses. "Many more instances of blatant scams and economic mismanagement have been covered in the White Paper on the Indian Economy released in February 2024. It remains relevant even now," she said.

On Thursday, the finance ministry said the entire valuation methodology used in the stake sale of IDBI Bank was reviewed by the core group of secretaries on disinvestment (CGD). In a 'Clarification on the Process of Strategic Restructuring of IDBI' issued on Thursday, the ministry said in due exercise of these powers, the CGD itself determined the procedure for the second or the best offer round. Earlier this week, Sitharaman criticised Gandhi over his comments on the Tata Group, accusing him of politicising commercial and legal matters. "Casually labelling commercial and legal matters as criminal is unacceptable," Sitharaman said on X.

data.title: Rel Retail Q2 Profit Declines on Qcomm Push
data.description:
Our Bureau Kolkata: Reliance Retail Ventures on Friday reported a 24.5% year-on-year decline in net profit to 2,619 crore for the quarter ended September, even as revenue from operations rose 5.8% to 80,220 crore. Its fast-moving consumer goods business, run under Reliance Consumer Products, saw gross revenue surge 1.6 times on year to 8,266 crore. India's largest retailer attributed the hit on profitability for a third straight quarter to planned investments in quick commerce such as dark stores, along with absorbing input cost rise to shield demand and a shift in the festive season compared to last year.

It said in the earnings call that the share of ecommerce to total grocery and fashion sales have gone up, and expect to drive value from ecommerce in FY28 and FY29. The company cited the festive season shift for the muted revenue growth as well. Despite that, the business achieved a 7% year-on-year (YoY) growth in transactions during the quarter, it noted.

Gross revenue rose 6.4% year on year to 91,716 crore after adjusting for the demerger of the consumer brands business in December last year. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda), before one-time impairment charge of 108 crore from closure of 7-Eleven stores, was at 6,228 crore was down 8.6% YoY, while Ebitda margin stood at 7.8%. The company said finance costs went up 53.9% YoY at 905 crore due to higher borrowing and interest rates. Reliance Retail Ventures executive director Isha M Ambani said the company is building a future-ready retail business by combining an extensive physical network with digital convenience, technology and a deep understanding of Indian consumers. "The new model with fast growing digital commerce and B2B channels is working and funded by the profits of offline business," she said.

Reliance Retail opened 303 stores during last quarter with a net reduction of 222 stores sequentially over the first quarter due to closure of unproductive stores. The company's total store count was at 19,947 as of September. Mukesh D Ambani, chairman and MD of Reliance Industries, said in a media statement the retail business posted sustained growth across all formats and channels. "Consumer demand stayed healthy, supported by our extensive physical and digital presence and our continued focus on serving the diverse needs of Indian consumers," he said.

data.title: Inflation Hurts Mass-mkt Liquor Portfolio: USL CEO
data.description:
Aanya Thakur Mumbai: Inflation and a weaker monsoon are weighing on lower-income urban consumers, posing a challenge for United Spirits as the Diageo-controlled liquor maker seeks to revive growth in its mass-market portfolio while banking on premiumisation to drive sales. "India 1, the bottom end, the India 1 consumer, which is a target audience for the lower half of the IMFL portfolio, is showing signs of fatigue due to the impact of inflation on their wallets," chief executive Praveen Someshwar said during the company's September-quarter earnings call. "India 2 and India 3 are robust and holding up." The strain is also visible in the company's lower-priced portfolio, where regulatory changes are adding additional pressures.

United Spirits' popular segment reported a 22.7% decline in net sales value to 181 crore in the quarter, accounting for about 6% of revenue. The business was hit by adverse policy changes in Maharashtra and Karnataka.

The company's prestige and above portfolio grew 6%, making up 94% of revenue. The Smirnoff maker said it has no immediate plans to intervene in its popular portfolio, largely comprising McDowell's rum, even as CFO Pradeep Jain acknowledged that future profit and growth pools lay in higher-priced brands. "The category will probably die a natural death, so as of now we don't want to make any interventions," he added.

Cost inflation is another pressure point. The West Asia conflict has added about 50 crore to costs in the quarter, affecting glass, energy, packaging and logistics. Extra neutral alcohol prices have also started rising on account of El NiÃ±o's impact on monsoons and crop inflation, the company said.

It expects lower Scotch import duties under the India-UK free trade agreement to offset the ENA cost in the coming quarter. "Hopefully, this will be neutralised by the full effect of the FTA benefit," said Jain, adding that impact beyond the next quarter was "very difficult to call out." The FTA benefit comes amid a directorate of revenue intelligence investigation into the classification of Scotch imports.

data.title: Suzlon Cuts Operating Margin Guidance to 15%
data.description:
Kalpana Pathak Mumbai: Wind energy major Suzlon Energy has cut its FY27 operating margin guidance to 15%, down from its earlier projection of 17%, as an unfavourable project mix, rising commodity costs, and foreign exchange volatility put pressure on profitability. Its earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (Ebitda) margin stood at 15.1% in the first half of FY27.

Management expects margins to improve as non-recurring operating expenses taper off and business volumes increase following the monsoon season. "The order book, even after high execution, remains at a healthy 6 GW, which is almost a year and a half of order book in hand. India is a great market growing from 8GW to 13GW in the next couple of years," Ajay Kapur, CEO, Suzlon Group, told ET. The wind turbine maker is counting on a sharp pick-up in deliveries in the second half of the fiscal year to improve operating leverage, while gearing up to enter overseas markets with its next-generation turbines.

The company estimates that non-recurring operating expenses have affected margins by about one percentage point, while foreign exchange movements and commodity-related pressures linked to geopolitical tensions have had an estimated 0.5 percentage point impact. Suzlon Energy reported a 1.3% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to 394 crore for the September quarter of FY27.

Net profit in the year-ago quarter stood at 389 crore, excluding a deferred tax benefit of 891 crore that had taken reported profit to 1,279 crore. Changes in the mix of customers and projects have also weighed on its performance. The company expects the impact of non-recurring expenses to taper in the third and fourth quarters.

A reduction in commodity price pressures could provide further upside to margins, Kapur added. Geopolitical tensions, including the possibility of further conflict in the Middle East, could increase input costs. However, Suzlon believes its predominantly domestic supply chain offers some insulation compared with manufacturers that rely more heavily on imports.

data.title: GAIL Q2 Profit Up Over Twofold at 4,650 cr Despite Global Disruptions
data.description:
Our Bureau New Delhi: GAIL (India) more than doubled its September quarter net profit at 4,650 crore from 2,217 crore a year earlier as global energy supply disruptions triggered by the West Asia crisis sharply boosted gas marketing margins.

Revenue from operations at the state-run gas transporter surged 31% year-on-year to 45,924 crore. The company's board, which met Friday, approved listing of wholly owned subsidiary GAIL Gas, a city gas distributor, by diluting up to 25% of its stake. It also cleared a proposal to transfer six city gas licensed areas to GAIL Gas through a slump sale with effect from January 1, 2027, according to a regulatory filing.

Operating profit from GAIL's natural gas marketing business jumped two-and-a-half times to 3,284 crore in the September quarter from 1,304 crore a year earlier. Operating profit from gas transmission rose 36% to 1,926 crore, while profit from the LPG and other liquid hydrocarbons business nearly quadrupled to 442 crore.

Losses in the petrochemicals business narrowed to 22 crore from 299 crore a year earlier. The Iran war and the near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz have disrupted energy flows from the Gulf. Petronet LNG, a key supplier of Qatari LNG to GAIL, declared force majeure on March 3. Since then, GAIL hasn't received any Qatari volumes from Petronet, the company said. The improved earnings lifted the stock 1.7% to 168 apiece on the BSE, outperforming a 0.42% rise in the benchmark Sensex.

data.title: JioStar Net Profit Falls 13% to 1,147 crore in Sept Qtr
data.description:
Mumbai: JioStar, the media and entertainment arm of Reliance Industries (RIL), reported a 13% year-on-year decline in net profit at 1,147 crore in the September quarter, compared to 1,322 crore a year earlier.

Gross revenue rose 9.8% to 7,944 crore, while revenue from operations increased 10% to 6,806 crore, according to RIL's investor presentation. However, Ebitda from operations fell 10.5% to 1,372 crore. Operating Ebitda margin contracted 600 basis points to 22.1%. Total Ebitda, including investment income, declined 13.6% to 1,502 crore.

JioHotstar averaged around 440 million monthly active users during the quarter, up 10% year-on-year, while entertainment watch-time grew more than 15%. Active subscribers in Singapore, the UK and Canada rose around 30% following the platform's September relaunch in these markets.

JioHotstar introduced "Pay Kisi Aur Se" or "Ask Others to Pay", allowing subscribers to ask friends or family to complete their payments. The company said the feature led to a 10% increase in incremental payment initiations. It also extended CTV access to mobile plan users, with viewing limited to two hours a month. The six editions of 'Bigg Boss' collectively reached more than 90 million viewers in their first three weeks.- Our Bureau

data.title: ZEE Profit Falls 40% in Q2, Revenue Rises on FIFA Subscription Growth
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: Zee Entertainment Enterprises (ZEE) reported a 40% year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit at 46 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, even as operating revenue rose 13% to 2,225 crore, driven by subscription growth aided by the FIFA World Cup 2026.

Ebitda fell 52% to 71 crore, pulling the margin down to 3.2% from 7.4% a year earlier, as higher programming and promotional costs weighed on profitability. Total expenditure rose 18% to 2,154 crore, with operating expenses increasing 14% to 1,225 crore and advertising and promotion (A&P) spends surging 55% to 571 crore.

The increase reflected FIFA-related programming costs and investments in initiatives such as Bullet and Music. Advertising revenue remained flat at 803 crore, while subscription revenue grew 30% to 1,332 crore. Domestic advertising was supported by FIFA, marquee shows such as Sa Re Ga Ma Pa and fresh content launches.

The company expects the festive season to aid advertising growth. FIFA 2026 and a strong content pipeline also drove higher digital average revenue per user (ARPU) and subscriber growth. ZEE5 revenue more than doubled 101% to 626 crore, while Ebitda turned positive at 42 crore against a loss of 31 crore a year earlier.

The platform released 34 shows and movies, including nine originals, during the quarter, maintaining stable usage and engagement. Zee's TV network share stood at 20% in week 24 of 2026, its highest in more than 7 years. Television ratings remain suspended following the ministry of information and broadcasting's direction to the Broadcast Audience Research Council India to comply with the TV Ratings Guidelines 2026.

data.title: Varun Beverages Q3 Net Up 13%, but Margins Fall
data.description:
Our Bureau New Delhi: Varun Beverages (VBL), PepsiCo's second-largest franchise bottler globally, reported 13.5% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit at 830.6 crore for the July-September 2026 quarter, but the company's shares fell 4.39% to hit an intraday low of 396.5 apiece after it reported a moderation in operating margins.

VBL, which follows a calendar year, said in an exchange filing that sales were driven by double-digit volume growth in India and international markets. It said revenue from operations increased 33.3% to 6,815.6 crore in the quarter under consideration. On a standalone basis, the company reported revenue from operations at 3,822.4 crore, up 24.75% on-year. However, the bottling company reported a gross margin decline by 334 bps to 53.1% in the quarter, on account of higher packaging material costs for shrink films and cans, driven by geopolitical disruptions.

VBL said in a management commentary that surge in prices of sugar was offset by increase in low sugar/no sugar products, which grew from 44% in Q3 CY2025, to as high as 88% in the July-September 2026 quarter. It said consolidated sales volume grew 28.7% to 354.4 million cases in the quarter under consideration, compared to 275.3 million cases in the corresponding year-ago quarter.

The company attributed the numbers to robust volume growth of 22.5% in India and 39.9% in its international markets. On October 14, Nestle India too reported standalone net profit increase of 36% year-on-year for the quarter ended September at 1,027 crore, but its stock plunged 7.76% after it flagged food inflation and commodity cost pressures as key concerns.

Earlier this year, VBL extended its exclusive bottling and trademark license agreement with PepsiCo till April 30, 2049, replacing its earlier term which had been valid till April 30, 2039. It also inked a revised deal with PepsiCo at the same time.

data.title: 'Gone Haywire' for Reopening Settled Issue, SC Slams Aptel
data.description:
New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday said the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (Aptel) had "gone haywire" for reopening an already settled issue, holding it to be in "blatant breach of judicial discipline and in clear violation of Article 141 of the Constitution of India".

Setting aside a 2024 review order by Aptel that cut down the tariff treatment allowed to Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC), a bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran said the quasi-judicial body reopened a question already settled by the top court. "We are apologetic for the expression but we find no substitute to express our angst in allowing the review, that too, when the very same issue, for the earlier years, was settled by this court in Bhaskar Shrachi Alloys (case), based on which, the original order was passed by the tribunal," bench said.

According to Article 141 of the Constitution, the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all Indian courts. Orders like the one passed by Aptel raise doubts in the minds of judges about independence vis-Ã -vis accountability, the top court said. It imposed exemplary costs of 2 lakh on Maithan Alloys, which filed the review petition before the appellate tribunal, and 1.5 lakh on public sector Steel Authority of India for supporting the review. The fines must be paid to DVC within one month, failing which an interest of 18% per annum shall be applied, the top court said.

data.title: Spandana Makes 18-cr Profit in Q2
data.description:
Kolkata: Microfinance company Spandana Sphoorty Financial reported a consolidated net profit of 18 crore for the second quarter of the fiscal, compared with 12 crore in the first quarter and a loss o 249 crore in the year-ago period.

The standalone net profit for the quarter under review, which reflects earnings from its microfinance operations, stood at 35 crore against a loss of 218 crore in the corresponding period last year. The consolidated pre-provision operating profit stood at 79 crore against a loss of 40 crore in the year-ago quarter.

data.title: New India Slips into Red on Underwriting Losses
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: New India Assurance Company (NIACL) reported a net loss of 1,267 crore in the September quarter, against a net profit of 63 crore in the corresponding period last year, as underwriting losses widened amid adverse claims experience in property, motor and health insurance.

Gross written premium (GWP) rose 5.2% year on year to 11,083 crore from 10,541 crore, the state-owned general insurer said in its earnings release. "This second quarter has been one of the most challenging quarters for the company in recent times, more so while succeeding another equally challenging one for the entire industry," said Lavanya R Mundayur, chairman and MD. "This quarter, GWP grew by only 5.1%, primarily due to the steep decline in property rates. " Net premium written increased marginally by 0.5% to 8,850 crore, while net premium earned grew 2.5% to 9,632 crore. Underwriting loss widened to 5,237 crore in the quarter from 3,554 crore a year earlier.
